task: T2: create .github/workflows/build-images.yml. This repository has no .github directory yet, so create it. The workflow builds and pushes container images to GHCR, and it is modelled on a known-good workflow that does exactly this job in this environment — described in full here, since it lives in another repository you cannot read. It triggers on `push` to the `main` branch, filtered by `paths` so an unrelated commit does not rebuild: the list must include `docker/**` and the workflow's own path `.github/workflows/build-images.yml`. It declares top-level `permissions` of `contents: read` and `packages: write` — no more. It has one job running on `ubuntu-latest` with a `strategy.matrix` whose single entry today carries three values: the image name `loop-executor`, the Dockerfile path `docker/loop-executor.Dockerfile`, and the version-file path `docker/loop-executor.VERSION`; a second image must be addable as one more matrix entry and nothing else. The steps in order: `actions/checkout@v4`; a step that reads the matrix entry's version file into a step output; `docker/setup-qemu-action@v3` (this is what makes an arm64 build possible on an amd64 runner, so it is not optional); `docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`; `docker/login-action@v3` against registry `ghcr.io` with username `${{ github.actor }}` and password `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`; and `docker/build-push-action@v6` with `context: .`, `file` set to the matrix Dockerfile, `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64`, `push: true`, and `tags` set to `ghcr.io/mtgibbs/<image>:<version>` built from the matrix entry and the version output. Do NOT tag `latest`: a mutable tag gives Flux nothing to compare and gives an incident no way to say which commit is running. Add a header comment recording that the GHCR package must be flipped public after the first push, with the exact command `gh api -X PATCH /user/packages/container/loop-executor -f visibility=public`. Create only this file.
